title: Rewrite the Correlated Subquery
statement: This correlated-subquery pattern correctly finds every product priced above the average price of its own category, but it's slow: the subquery re-scans `products` and recomputes the category average once per outer row. `SELECT p.name, p.category, p.price FROM products p WHERE p.price > (SELECT AVG(p2.price) FROM products p2 WHERE p2.category = p.category);` Write an equivalent query that returns the exact same rows (same three columns) by joining `products` to a pre-aggregated per-category average instead of using a correlated subquery (no window functions either). Row order does not matter.
starter_code:
SELECT p.name, p.category, p.price
FROM products p
JOIN (
  SELECT category, AVG(price) AS avg_price
  FROM products
  GROUP BY category
) -- TODO: alias the derived table and complete the JOIN condition
WHERE -- TODO: compare p.price against the derived table's avg_price
;
hints: First compute a small per-category summary table with GROUP BY category, then JOIN the original products table to it on category
The toys category has only one product, priced exactly at its own (single-item) average, so it should NOT appear in the result
